title: Refund Human Trail
oneLiner: A consumer proof room for automated airline or retailer refund failures where broken forms, vanished support, and scam numbers create money-loss risk.
targetUser: Travelers and shoppers fighting automated refund systems, plus consumer advocates who help them file complaints.
keyUX: The user drops in emails, screenshots, failed form captures, call attempts, and charge details; the app builds a timeline, complaint packet, and safe human contact checklist.
requiredUISections: Refund case header with deadline, amount, merchant, and risk level.
Timeline builder for cancellation notice, failed form, emails, chats, calls, and complaint IDs.
Evidence upload grid grouped by proof type.
Scam-risk checker for phone numbers, search results, and suspicious payment asks.
Complaint packet generator for card dispute, regulator, merchant, or travel insurer.
Human-contact map with verified channels and escalation attempts.
Final checklist before filing or sharing the packet.
sourceSignalReferences: S7 - Wired, low-cost airline AI support creates refund/scam risk
S8 - Guardian, retail AI assistants risk going rogue or annoying customers
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app prototype called "Refund Human Trail" for consumers documenting automated refund failures. The first screen should be a case workspace, not marketing. Include refund case header, deadline and amount risk, timeline builder, evidence upload grid, scam-risk checker, complaint packet generator, verified human-contact map, and final filing checklist. Use realistic sample data from a canceled flight/refund form failure with emails, failed pages, and suspected fake support numbers. Design direction: use the financial-analyst profile with rigorous case evidence, restrained charts, confidence badges, ink/off-white surfaces, and calm warning tones.
